transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, my daughter actually made the appointment for me because she says I never sit down. And it's true, I feel like I’m always up and moving. Like, even on what's supposed to be a quiet day... oh, speaking of quiet days, Sunday was supposed to be my day of rest. The weather was just gorgeous, wasn't it? My neighbor Susan came by with these huge Meyer lemons from her sister's tree down in Florida. They make the absolute best pie, but you really have to use a lot of sugar, otherwise it's just too tart for my liking... 

Anyway, where was I? Oh, right. Even when I'm trying to have a quiet day, I'm just bouncing from my garden club list—I'm the secretary this year, which is a whole headache on its own—over to my knitting bag, and then I'm digging through my travel papers for this cruise I'm thinking about taking. I just end up doing all that before I’ve really finished any one thing. I just can't seem to just sit and be.
Has this restless, jump-from-task-to-task feeling started fairly recently, or is it something you've noticed your whole life, even back in childhood?

Oh, heavens, no, it's not recent at all. It’s been my whole life, really. Even back in grade school, I remember my teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright girl, but just so scattered. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn, and just... wiggling around in my seat before I ever finished my work. Especially during arithmetic. 

Oh, I couldn't stand arithmetic. My sister, Martha, though, she was an absolute whiz with numbers. She actually worked as a bookkeeper for Miller’s Hardware for... oh, it must have been thirty-five years. You know, the hardware store that used to be right on the corner of Elm and Main? Well, maybe you don't, they tore it down a few years back to put up one of those drive-through coffee places, which I just don't understand. The coffee is so bitter, and they charge you an arm and a leg for it! I still make mine at home with a percolator. It just tastes so much better, don't you think? Plus, you don't have to wait in that terrible line of cars spilling out into the street. 

But... wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, childhood. Yes, I've always been a bit of a wiggler, ever since I was a little girl.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes lifelong (since early childhood) symptoms of hyperactivity (restlessness, inability to sit still, jumping between tasks), impulsivity (talking out of turn), and inattention (losing papers, difficulty finishing tasks, distractibility, tangential thought patterns during the interview). These symptoms have been persistent since grade school, are pervasive across settings (home, garden club, family life), and are causing noticeable functional concern (daughter arranged the appointment due to observable restlessness). There is no evidence of discrete mood episodes, elevated/irritable mood, grandiosity, or decreased need for sleep that would suggest a manic or hypomanic episode, making bipolar disorder less likely. The chronic, early-onset, cross-situational nature of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity is most consistent with Hyperkinetic Disorder (ADHD, Combined Presentation) F90.0.
